name: Babak · baseline chaser
pattern: Patrol, recognise the player, chase, turn and visibly give up.
adaptation: Give Russet Bull and our ground enemies a complete notice → pursuit → failed attack → recovery vocabulary.
rigNotes: 47 source skin joints; body, head and limbs carry distinct motion. Compare turn and give-up clips before redesigning the silhouette.
caveat: Navigation and inherited enemy states are outside the clips; a new local controller must own travel and collision.

name: Lurker Crab · exposure window
pattern: Alternates protected movement with an exposed peek; snip and kickback supply readable combat punctuation.
adaptation: Turn Coral Crab into a defensive sideways patrol with a deliberate opening and a visible recoil.
rigNotes: Separate claws, legs and body; inspect peek, idle-to-walk and peek-to-walk as well as the walking loop.
caveat: Our current crab is an ordinary patrol target. Changing its vulnerability is a future gameplay decision, not part of this audit.

name: Aphid Lurker · deployable spikes
pattern: Normal and deadly walks are separate clips; spikes deploy and the enemy gives up.
adaptation: Replace always-on spike danger with an unmistakable raised/lowered threat state.
rigNotes: Spine/spike articulation must preserve the silhouette and show the dangerous surface before it becomes active.
caveat: The export plays the motion; it does not import invulnerability flags or their timing.

name: Jungle Hopper · distinct jump sizes
pattern: Short and long jumps have separate landing clips, with idle and burp personality beats.
adaptation: Give Spring Frog an anticipatory short hop, a committed long leap and a weighty finite landing.
rigNotes: 39 skin joints. Assess pelvis compression, hind-leg extension, foreleg landing and mouth motion separately.
caveat: Jump arcs and ground selection come from the controller; an in-place clip does not prove reachable landings.

name: Quicksand Lurker · pop-up shooter
pattern: Hides when approached, rises to track, then spits a projectile from its animated mouth.
adaptation: Develop an organic sentry with hide → emerge → aim → fire → recoil, preserving a safe approach opportunity.
rigNotes: 49 joints and eight clips, including hide, popup and spit. Mouth/socket alignment is essential.
caveat: The projectile, hiding translation and aim logic are separate from this mesh. No projectile or damage is simulated in the viewer.

name: Swamp Bat · swoop and return
pattern: Launches from an idle group into swoop, strafe and return phases.
adaptation: Give Violet Watcher a visible launch cue, committed attack pass and distinct recovery path.
rigNotes: A compact 16-joint wing rig and six clips; preserve the complete wing silhouettes.
caveat: The source uses a group/path host. The clip viewer does not reconstruct that host or its flight paths.

name: Driller Lurker · attack and jam
pattern: Path patrol and chase lead into a drill attack, followed by a jammed standing state.
adaptation: Create a heavy lane blocker whose attack exhausts into an obvious punishable jam.
rigNotes: 67 joints; paired level/up walk, run and attack clips offer a useful slope/aim blending study.
caveat: The 12-clip Robocave export is chosen deliberately; the historical Maincave export had no clips. Aim blending and path motion remain unimplemented.

name: Bully · spin and dizziness
pattern: Starts spinning, reacts to collisions and slows into a dizzy pause.
adaptation: Evolve Brass Whirler into windup → dangerous sweep → deceleration → vulnerable recovery.
rigNotes: 44 joints with spin-start, spin, bounce and dizzy poses; body/root rotation is also controller-driven.
caveat: A spin clip alone is not the complete rotating attack. The audit does not import travel, bounce or combat rules.

name: Kermit · tongue attacker
pattern: Hops into range, lashes a tongue, then holds or retracts after a hit/miss decision.
adaptation: A new reach attacker could punish a predictable line while offering escape and a long recovery.
rigNotes: 28 joints; eight authored clips. The tongue uses additional runtime control beyond the stored skeleton animation.
caveat: Higher effort: tongue targeting, stretch, clearance, attachment and release require original implementation. The source clip alone is incomplete.

name: Baby Spider · spawned pursuer
pattern: Birth, notice, walk/run, jump/land and death form a useful small pursuer vocabulary.
adaptation: Prototype a few readable ground pursuers before increasing swarm density.
rigNotes: 21 joints; nine clips with separate jump/landing and appearance motion.
caveat: Leg contact and multiple-agent spacing need new tests; more instances are not a substitute for readable attacks.

name: Mother Spider · spawner and spitter
pattern: Lowers into an encounter, produces offspring, spits and reacts to hits.
adaptation: A later encounter anchor can alternate spawning, ranged pressure and an exposed recovery.
rigNotes: 29 joints; ten clips include birth, lowering, spit and multiple death/leg variants.
caveat: Eggs, children, detached legs and uppercut-specific death need additional hosts/parts. Not a one-mesh drop-in.

name: Jungle Snake · short/long strike
pattern: Coiled idle, close/far strikes, drop-down and give-up communicate reach.
adaptation: Use the close/far strike distinction to improve Moa anticipation, or make a new stationary reach enemy.
rigNotes: 26 joints. Evaluate the coiled animated pose; the unposed chain is much longer.
caveat: The bind pose is not a useful size reference. Strike reach and hit volumes must be authored separately.

name: Lurker Worm · ground ambush
pattern: Idle, rise, chomp and sink form an emergence ambush.
adaptation: Add a visible ground tell followed by one committed bite and retreat.
rigNotes: 15 joints and five clips; a small rig for a strong silhouette change.
caveat: Ground concealment, damage window and emergence trigger are controller responsibilities.

name: Bone Lurker · directional charge
pattern: Chase vocabulary adds left/right charge variants and a stun.
adaptation: Study curved pursuit presentation and a readable stunned state for a future biped enemy.
rigNotes: 58 joints; 14 clips. Check carried attachments and directional body lean.
caveat: Do not retarget directly to the bull: anatomy and joint meaning differ.

name: Lurker Puppy · small runner
pattern: Walk, run, jump, landing and celebration provide a compact animated pursuer.
adaptation: An alternative small quadruped direction with stronger run/stop variety than a single gait.
rigNotes: 31 joints and seven clips; compare gait and takeoff contacts.
caveat: Requires new contact mapping and a controller; current source mesh is only a placeholder.

name: Gnawer · task-driven creature
pattern: Moves between idle, run, notice, chewing/tugging and hit responses.
adaptation: A creature attacking scenery could create an objective beyond touching the player.
rigNotes: 36 joints, 12 clips, including chewing transitions and separate segment motion.
caveat: Segment pieces and interaction targets are not assembled by the clip player.

name: Snow Bunny · hopping attacker
pattern: Small/big hops, spotting/landing, attack and death create a compact hop-based opponent.
adaptation: Alternative hop proportions and a clear notice beat for Spring Frog studies.
rigNotes: 21 joints; seven clips. Full exported mesh is only 332 triangles, not a distance-generated substitute.
caveat: Frog anatomy needs a new rig and weight pass even if timing is adopted.

name: Citadel Bunny · hop variant
pattern: Citadel variation on idle, big/small hop, notice, attack and death.
adaptation: Compare timing and silhouette with Snow Bunny before counting it as a new role.
rigNotes: 21 joints and seven clips; distinct source mesh/animation names.
caveat: An art/variant study, not evidence of a wholly different enemy archetype.

name: Yeti · heavy chaser
pattern: Idle/walk, spot, charge, give-up, turn and land sell a heavier chaser.
adaptation: Study body mass, slower anticipation and recovery in a new heavy silhouette.
rigNotes: 47 joints and 11 clips; compare with Babak without assuming identical weights.
caveat: Similar chase vocabulary; avoid spending a roster slot on only a larger reskin.

name: Green Eco Lurker · arena chaser

caveat: Its arena host and spawn logic are not part of the clip set.

name: Swamp Rat · nest runner
pattern: Fall/bounce, walk/run, notice and eating give a nest-launched runner personality.

name: Double Lurker · stacked pair
pattern: A stacked duo can take hits, break apart and resume as separate participants.

rigNotes: 32-joint lower model and a separate 30-joint upper model; both have 14 clips.
caveat: Requires two actor lifecycles, attachment sockets, split collision and synchronised clips; preview shows one mesh at a time.

name: Double Lurker · upper partner
pattern: Upper partner supplies on-shoulders, hit, split and solo motion.

caveat: Must be paired with the lower actor before claiming assembled fidelity.

name: Ram Boss · directional shield
pattern: Forward/up defence, block, throw and shield-loss states support directional counterplay.
adaptation: Adapt only the directional guard and shield-break pattern for a manageable armoured enemy.
rigNotes: 44 joints and 21 clips; shield/no-shield and dismount variants need semantic selection.
caveat: A multi-phase encounter rather than a simple turtle swap; mounts and projectiles are additional dependencies.

name: Balloon Lurker · mounted flyer

caveat: The pilot and flight path are separate dependencies; not a rich standalone flight set.
